fault: Slot reading, debrief turned-how line 2: "{who} said yes. It took {approach} for {price}." fills as "It took ask for $0." and "It took pay for $70,000." This is the same verb-in-slot problem as last round, now only in the second variant. "It took help" and "It took pressure" read, but ask and pay do not.
fix: Reword so every verb reads, e.g. "{who} said yes to the {approach} approach, for {price}." or "{who} said yes. Approach: {approach}, at {price}."

fault: Slot reading, debrief give-up line 2: "{who} told investigators {fact}." fills as "told investigators the Fixer's face". One cannot tell someone a face. The facts given are fixer-face, cell-car and place-time, so the line misreads for the most common fact.
fix: Use a verb that takes all three facts, as line 1 does: "{who} gave investigators {fact}. {left} against {right}." or "...described {fact}...".

fault: Temperament fit, idealist read: "Help, not pay. That is the only way in." The Temperament Spec says an Idealist under a Hero campaign "Volunteers with no offer needed", so Help is not the only way in. The Scout's read would mislead the player, as the old loyal read did.
fix: Drop the absolute, e.g. "Help, not pay. Money insults them." or "Won't be bought. Help works."

fault: Position job, usher: "seat the queue" fills "I seat the queue." No one seats a queue: an usher shows people to their seats or keeps the queue in order. The line reads oddly for every usher.
fix: Use e.g. "show people to their seats" or "keep the queue moving".
